artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice and let $J=J(L)$ denote the set of join-irreducible elements of $L$, equipped with the partial order induced from $L$. Define the map
$$\rho_L:J\times J\to 2^{J},\qquad \rho_L(a,b)=\{c\in J:\ c\le a\vee b\}.$$
It is known that the pair $(J,\rho_L)$ determines $L$ up to isomorphism: if $L_1$ and $L_2$ are finite modular lattices and there is an order isomorphism $J(L_1)\to J(L_2)$ that intertwines $\rho_{L_1}$ and $\rho_{L_2}$, then $L_1\cong L_2$.

Problem. Given a finite poset $(P,\le)$ and a function $\rho:P\times P\to 2^{P}$, find necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions on $(P,\rho)$ guaranteeing the existence of a finite modular lattice $L$ together with an order isomorphism $P\to J(L)$ under which $\rho$ corresponds to $\rho_L$. Equivalently, characterize intrinsically the pairs $(P,\rho)$ that arise from finite modular lattices.
artifact.status_search_result: The encoding of a finite modular lattice by its poset of join-irreducibles together with the join-closure function is due to Faigle–Herrmann (1981) and has been further studied via "bases of lines" and tight embeddings into partition lattices. Recent literature (Herrmann's "Modular lattices of finite length" parts A/B; Faigle–Herrmann–Wild on tight embeddings) treats partial geometric characterizations and acyclicity criteria but does not provide a complete intrinsic characterization of the data $(J,\rho)$ corresponding to a modular lattice. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Tight embedding of modular lattices into partition lattices: progress and program
status_evidence.snippet: Bases of lines attempt to describe a modular lattice geometrically; the point set is J(L) and lines are maximal sets of join-irreducibles with the same join.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric descriptions of modular lattices via join-irreducibles remain an active research program without a complete classification.

status_evidence.title: Modular lattices of finite length (Part B)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of structural results on modular lattices of finite length, building on Faigle–Herrmann.
status_evidence.claim: No intrinsic axiomatization of the function rho characterizing modular lattices is given.

status_evidence.title: On the number of join irreducibles and acyclicity in finite modular lattices
status_evidence.snippet: A base of L is acyclic iff L has exactly 2d(L)-s(L) join irreducibles.
status_evidence.claim: Partial combinatorial characterizations exist (acyclic case), but a full classification remains unresolved.
